questions.q: What format is a fine-tuning training file, with one example conversation per line?
questions.explain: JSONL (one JSON object per line) is the standard shape — each line is a full {"messages": [...]} example.

questions.q: What two fields are required to create a fine-tuning job in OpenAI's API?
questions.explain: model (the base model) and training_file (the uploaded file ID) are required; hyperparameters are optional overrides on top of sane defaults.

questions.q: What field does a successful fine-tuning job return that you then use to call the model?
questions.explain: fine_tuned_model is the new model ID string — you call it in the exact same chat completion shape as any other model.

questions.q: Which hyperparameters can you optionally override on an OpenAI fine-tuning job?
questions.explain: These nest under method.supervised.hyperparameters — the recommended default is to leave them alone unless you have a specific, measured reason to change them.

questions.q: How does fine-tuning a Claude model differ structurally from fine-tuning a GPT model?
options: It's identical — same endpoint shape, different model string
Claude fine-tuning runs through Amazon Bedrock, not a self-serve Claude API call
Claude models cannot be fine-tuned under any circumstances
Claude fine-tuning requires no training data at all
questions.explain: As covered in Lesson 20, Anthropic's own Claude API has no self-serve fine-tuning endpoint; the real path runs through Amazon Bedrock or professional services.
